data.content_ref: inline:The integration's own refutation condition concedes the central fault: the two mechanisms (error cancellation from SRC_003, shared anchoring from SRC_002) may be 'not separable' and operate 'simultaneously and non-additively.' If so, the claimed integration — a conditional synthesis with a clean bias-threshold boundary — is not a substantive relation but an imposed dichotomy that the underlying phenomena do not support. The target names the kind as 'integration' yet its own refutation-if admits the integration may be formally impossible because no well-defined boundary exists between the two regimes. A relation whose defining condition is possibly nonexistent is not substantively proposed; it is hypothesized and simultaneously withdrawn.
